newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris judge opens inquiry into Lagardere chairman.
newsitem.headline: Paris judge opens inquiry into Lagardere chairman.

text.p: A Paris magistrate specialising in white-collar crime has decided to open an investigation into industrialist Jean-Luc Lagardere following a complaint by a minority shareholder, justice sources said on Thursday.

Eva Joly is following up a complaint filed against against terms of a 1992 merger between Matra Defense Espace, the defence unit of Lagardere Groupe, and media group Hachette. Lagardere is chairman of the company named after him.
Joly's action contradicted the public prosecutor's view that there were no grounds for a prosecution following a commercial court's ruling against the complaint.
Joly has the power to pursue the case as the lawsuit was filed as a civil action with a claim for damages, the sources said.

They said the judge would place Lagardere under criminal investigation for alleged "misappropriation of company assets, embezzlement and fraud". That is the first stage to prosecution but does not automatically lead to a trial.

Newspaper Le Monde said a Matra shareholder, Jean-Pierre Malen, brought the action arguing that the merger terms were unfavourable because certain contracts were not disclosed to minority stockholders in Matra.

Lagardere faces a separate investigation, opened on October 28 by magistrate Andre Dando, following complaints on control exercised over Matra Hachette by the Lagardere group and a system of fees paid to its managers.
The government has picked Lagardere as its preferred buyer in the privatisation of the Thomson SA electronics firm, subject to European Commission and French privatisation commission approval.
The sale of Thomson for a symbolic one franc, and a planned disposal to Daewoo Electronics of South Korea, has sparked political and trade union opposition.
